open_points.subject: A16 request validation order
open_points.text: A16 rule 1: "A request is handled in this order ... its token is known; it fits the operation's schema ..."; A16 rule 4: "Every request is validated against its schema before anything else happens".
open_points.question: Which check runs first when both token and schema are invalid: token check or schema validation?
options: Follow rule 1 order (token before schema)
Follow rule 4 statement (schema before anything)
open_points.default_guess: Follow rule 1's explicit ordered list and treat rule 4's phrase as non-literal.

open_points.subject: Adding trial cases vs owner capture
open_points.text: A04 rule 1: "A trial case is added only by an agent with the author right"; State 0 primary action: "capture a failed execution into the trial corpus | owner, agent with author right".
open_points.question: May the owner add a trial case via capture, or are all additions restricted to authoring agents?
options: Owner and authoring agent may add captured cases
Only authoring agents may add any trial case, including captured
open_points.default_guess: Allow owner capture as stated in State 0 and treat A04 rule 1 as applying to authored additions.

open_points.subject: Flow constants targeting same input
open_points.text: A05 phase 2 validates each constant target and schema fit, but no rule forbids multiple constants to the same `(to_node,to_port)`.
open_points.question: If two constants target one input port, is the flow refused, or which constant is used?
options: Refuse as ambiguous fan-in
Allow and pick first by constant order
Allow only if equal values

open_points.subject: Edge + constant to one input
open_points.text: A05 phase 6 forbids "no two edges that can both deliver" but is silent on a constant and an edge both ending at the same input port.
open_points.question: Can a constant and an edge both feed one input, and if yes which value is delivered?
options: Refuse any edge+constant double-delivery
Constant overrides edge
Edge overrides constant
open_points.default_guess: Refuse double-delivery to keep single-source inputs.

open_points.subject: Sandbox file-open trap vs runtime reads
open_points.text: A03 rule 4 installs an audit hook raising on "opening any path outside the exchange directory"; A03 rule 1 also allows a mounted read-only runtime.
open_points.question: Are reads from the mounted runtime (stdlib/import files) allowed after the hook is installed, or does the hook block them?
options: Allow runtime-path opens, block other host paths
Block all non-exchange opens literally
open_points.default_guess: Allow runtime-path opens (otherwise normal imports break).

open_points.subject: Sandbox trap coverage for time/random APIs
open_points.text: A03 rule 4: "replaces every clock and randomness entry point ... (`time`, `datetime` current-time functions, `os.urandom`, `random` seeding, `secrets`)".
open_points.question: Is this list exhaustive and normative, or illustrative with additional APIs to block?
options: Treat listed APIs as exact closed set
Treat list as examples and block any equivalent API found
open_points.default_guess: Treat as examples and block equivalent entry points too.

open_points.subject: Binding proposal shape check from schemas
open_points.text: A09 rule 2: "A binding whose ports cannot fit this shape by their schemas is refused when proposed".
open_points.question: What exact static criteria determine that a schema/port set "cannot fit" path/query/json/multipart placement?
options: Only basic type/category checks
Full schema satisfiability checks against transport shapes
Defer most checks to send time
open_points.default_guess: Do conservative basic type/category checks at proposal time and refuse clear mismatches.

open_points.subject: Transport error mapping boundary
open_points.text: A09 rule 5 distinguishes "nothing could be sent" vs "request may have been sent, no complete answer" but does not define mapping for concrete client-library/network errors.
open_points.question: How are specific transport exceptions (e.g., write timeout, TLS alert after bytes written, EOF before status) mapped to those two buckets?
options: Classify unknown/ambiguous send state as "may have been sent"
Classify by exception type heuristics
Classify all transport exceptions as "may have been sent" for non-read
open_points.default_guess: Use conservative rule: if send certainty is unavailable, treat as "may have been sent".

open_points.subject: Approval request deduplication for same waiting element
open_points.text: A10 rule 2 says the kernel "records an approval request" when authority is missing, but does not say whether repeated advances create new `requested` approvals or reuse one.
open_points.question: When the same run/node/element remains waiting for approval across multiple requests, is there one persistent approval request or many?
options: Exactly one active request per run/node/element/input digest
Create a new request each time the node is re-encountered
open_points.default_guess: Keep one active request per run/node/element/input digest.

open_points.subject: Attempt numbering across crash-before-record
open_points.text: A11 rule 1: "each execution ... takes the next number" and "every record about an attempt carries its number"; A14 rule 5 allows re-executing function elements that have no concluded record after restart.
open_points.question: If an execution occurred but crashed before any attempt-concluding record, must numbering skip that unseen attempt or reuse its number?
options: Numbers reflect only persisted/concluded attempts
Numbers must reflect every started attempt, including unrecorded starts
open_points.default_guess: Number by persisted attempt starts/conclusions so restart re-execution can use the next visible number consistently.

open_points.subject: Release-ceiling changes vs existing contracts
open_points.text: A20 rule 4: "A new release may change ceilings; recorded contract versions and executions keep the bounds they were issued and executed with."
open_points.question: After upgrade, may old contract versions whose bounds exceed new ceilings still execute/admit using their original bounds?
options: Yes, existing contracts keep executable old bounds
No, new release ceilings cap all future executions including old contracts
open_points.default_guess: Yes, preserve original contract bounds for existing versions.
